messages:
ana: FYI: we're instituting a short stability embargo next week to reduce risk during holiday traffic. Embargo window: 2025-12-24T00:00:00Z -> 2025-12-26T23:59:59Z. Only urgent bugfixes and security patches allowed.
kevin: What qualifies as urgent?
ana: Urgent = P0/P1 incidents affecting customer-facing traffic or security CVEs. Non-urgent perf work should wait.
release-coordinator: Exception workflow stays the same: submit the release-exception form and tag @release-coordinator. We'll target a 2-hour turnaround for pre-window exceptions.
sre-oncall: We're also enabling stricter canary thresholds for the embargo: p95 threshold lowered to 300ms and auto-abort on error_rate > 0.5% for 5m.
docs-bot: Added embargo page and checklist -> https://confluence.redwood/releases/embargo-2025-holiday (internal).
kevin: Any change to canary cadence?
release-coordinator: Yes 1% -> 10% -> 40% -> 100% with 20m observation at each step. We want slower ramp for network-sensitive services.
sre-oncall: Oncall rotation adjusted: primary + secondary will be paged for any auto-abort. If auto-abort fires, deployment will tag the commit and trigger an incident.
nana: Reminder: no non-critical image bumps after 2025-12-23T18:00:00Z. If you must push, fill the exception form with benchmarks and approval.
kevin: Will customer status page mention this?
release-coordinator: Short notice will go to status.redwood: "Stability embargo: no feature launches expected; emergency patches only." Dedicated customers on weekly maintenance lists will get a direct note.
sre-oncall: Pre-embargo smoke run planned 2025-12-23T20:00:00Z. I'll post results here.
nana: Thanks all 100. If you have planned releases that need to land before the embargo, submit exceptions now. Tag thread id 1805551234 for traceability.
kevin: Acked. Will reschedule a non-critical perf rollout.
